weeks.title: Quieting the alarm
weeks.description: Build a short, predictable routine that sends safety signals to the body, without over-analysis or facing painful memories.
weeks.focusTask: Log at the end of the day: activation, sleep, and one thing that helped.
weeks.outcome: Shorter activation, and a faster return to your baseline.
daily: Two minutes of orienting to the present.
Five minutes of calm breathing, or its substitute if breathing does not suit you.
Twenty to thirty minutes of movement.
Three short alarm check-ins during the day.
Eight to ten minutes of muscle release in the evening.
avoid: Do not try to analyse trauma or recall its details on your own.
Do not turn the measurement itself into a test you must pass.

weeks.title: Understanding the triggers
weeks.description: Separate immediate danger from elevated alarm, and notice one pattern a day rather than drowning in monitoring.
weeks.focusTask: Write one trigger entry, and reduce one safety behaviour slightly.
weeks.outcome: A clearer gap between the thought and the reality.
daily: Log one situation only: what happened, and what did your mind predict?
Write one piece of evidence for danger and one for a false alarm.
Pick one checking behaviour and reduce it gradually.
avoid: Do not turn the log into rumination or a running investigation.
Do not reduce any safety measure that is genuinely necessary in a dangerous environment.

weeks.title: Returning to life gradually
weeks.description: Pick a safe activity you have been avoiding, and return to it with a small repeatable step rather than jumping to the hardest situation.
weeks.focusTask: Do a safe activity rated 3 or 4 out of 10 for ten to twenty minutes.
weeks.outcome: The body learns that anxiety can pass without escape.
daily: Rank the avoided activities from 0 to 10.
Start with a moderately easy one and repeat it several times.
Allow some tension without seeking repeated reassurance.
avoid: Do not carry out exposure to traumatic memories on your own.
Do not make the goal the complete disappearance of anxiety during the activity.

weeks.title: Taking back the choice
weeks.description: Begin the day with a value you want to serve, and take a small action even while part of the alarm remains.
weeks.focusTask: Choose a value, then take one small step that serves it today.
weeks.outcome: Life does not wait for anxiety to reach zero.
daily: Choose a value: health, learning, a relationship, independence, creativity or another.
Write an action that takes five to twenty minutes and serves that value.
Do it while allowing some tension to be present.
Compare your progress with week one, kindly.
avoid: Do not use the comparison to punish yourself.
Do not treat a hard day as proof that all the progress is gone.
